transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I guess… the thing that finally made me come in is my eating’s gotten really inconsistent. Like some weeks I barely even touch dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed, eating crackers and sweets. It feels embarrassing to say, and I kept thinking it would just even out, but it hasn’t really.
After eating, do you ever make yourself sick or exercise a lot more than usual to try to balance it out?

I don’t think so… I mean, not in a planned way. I get upset with myself after, and sometimes I’ll clean the kitchen or walk around the house because I feel restless, but I’m not, like, making myself sick or doing workouts to undo it. I used to have a neighbor who would jog at night, actually, with one of those reflective vests, and I always thought that was brave because our streetlights are terrible—sorry, I’m getting off track. No, I haven’t really noticed myself doing that.
Do you ever feel like you’ve lost control while eating, like you can’t stop yourself once you start, especially during those times you’re eating late at night?

I think… yeah, sometimes it sort of feels that way, mostly at night. Like I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have a few crackers, and then I’m still standing there eating sweets too after everyone’s gone to bed. It’s not every night, because some weeks I barely even eat dinner, which is strange in the other direction.

Our kitchen light is really harsh at night, too, and I’ll notice every little crumb on the counter—sorry. But yes, that’s kind of what finally pushed me to come in, the eating being so all over the place.
Do these changes in your eating habits cause you a lot of distress, or make it hard for you to function normally in your daily life?

Yeah… it does, more than I want to admit. It’s not just the food, I think it sort of spills into everything. I’ve fallen behind on my facilitator training, and even my private blog stuff, because I can’t seem to organize the projects or explain things clearly like I used to.

And at home, the tension with my husband makes normal routines harder. Like even simple things—dinner, cleaning up, going to bed at a reasonable time—start feeling… tangled. I don’t know if that makes sense. I keep thinking if I could just get the days back into order, the eating would follow, but it hasn’t really worked that way.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like your blog or facilitator training?

Yes… I think so. Things I used to actually look forward to feel like these chores I keep putting off. Book club, for example—I’ll have the book sitting right there and somehow not pick it up.

And cooking, which used to be sort of calming for me, now feels like this whole production. Even going to galleries, or tending the rose beds outside… I used to love checking on them. My grandmother had roses too, these really stubborn pink ones that survived everything—anyway. Now I’ll look at mine and think, “I should do that,” and then I just don’t. It’s like the interest got dulled down.
Have you noticed a big drop in your energy level or felt unusually tired most days, even when you’re not doing much?

I’m not sure I’d call it a big drop, exactly. Some days I feel kind of worn out, but I have trouble telling if that’s actual tiredness or just… not getting myself moving.

Like yesterday I stood in front of a pile of towels for way too long because I couldn’t decide where to start, and then I got distracted by this loose thread on one of them—sorry, that’s not really the question. I guess I haven’t noticed being unusually exhausted most days, not in a clear way. It’s more muddled than that.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently, especially when you’re feeling down or stressed?

Yeah… that’s actually kind of what pushed me to come in. My eating has been really all over the place.

Some weeks I barely touch dinner, like I’ll make something or sit with everyone and then just sort of move food around. And then other nights, after everyone’s gone to bed, I’m standing in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets out of the cupboard. Not even like I planned to—I just end up there.

I don’t know about the weight exactly, I try not to hover around the scale too much, but the appetite part has definitely been… not normal for me.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or hopeless nearly every day, and it was hard to do even basic things like getting dressed or going to work?

I… I don’t know if I’ve counted it neatly as two weeks, but yes, I get these stretches where everything in the house feels gray and heavy. Like I’ll just sit at the kitchen table, staring at the same spot, feeling empty, even if nothing terrible happened that day.

It’s strange because the light in the kitchen changes in the afternoon and usually I notice that, or I’ll think about wiping the counters or making tea, and instead I just sit there. So… yes, down, I guess. Hopeless sometimes. It’s not always dramatic, it’s more like everything has gone flat.
Has there been a time when you didn’t feel any pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, even things that used to make you happy like cooking or tending to your rose beds?

Yes… yes, that happens. Things I used to actually look forward to, like book club or going to a gallery, now I’ll see them on the calendar and it feels like this heavy errand I should probably cancel.

And cooking too—I used to enjoy chopping things and getting the pan going, especially if the radio was on, but lately it’s like… why is there so much washing and deciding and standing there? Even the rose beds. I keep meaning to tend them, and then I notice the weeds and think I’ll do it tomorrow, and then tomorrow turns into… well, more tomorrows. So yes, it’s not that I hate those things, they just feel like chores I keep putting off.
Have you had days where you felt down or depressed most of the time, and it seemed like the sadness wouldn’t go away, even when nothing bad was happening?

Yes… I do. It’s not always because something happened, which is the part that makes me feel sort of foolish trying to explain it.

I’ll have these stretches where the whole house just feels gray and heavy, like even the walls are tired. I’ll sit at the kitchen table and just… sit there, feeling empty. Sometimes the kettle’s right there, or there are dishes I could do, and I’ll notice little things like a crumb on the counter, but I can’t seem to move myself into the day.

And nothing terrible has to have happened. It’s just there. Like the sadness settles in and doesn’t really lift.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or felt fatigued, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

I’m not sure. I mean… I don’t think of it as being tired exactly, like after carrying groceries or scrubbing the floor. It’s more that I’ll look at something and sort of put it off, but I don’t know if that’s energy or just… not getting started.

Sometimes I wonder if I’m just slow in the mornings. My mother used to say I moved like I was underwater, even when I was a kid, but she said a lot of things. So… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed fatigue in the way you mean, I guess.
Have you ever felt like you’re a failure or that you’ve let yourself or others down, especially during these low periods?

Yes… I do get that feeling. Not always in some big dramatic way, but I’ll do something small and then it becomes… enormous in my head.

Like, I bought this expensive tube of pigment once—well, not once, I mean, art supplies are just expensive now, it’s ridiculous—and I kept thinking, why did I do that, we didn’t need that, I’m selfish. And then suddenly it’s not about the paint anymore, it’s like I’ve damaged the whole household somehow.

Or if I snap at my spouse, even just a little, I’ll replay it for hours. The exact tone, what I should’ve said, how I’ve made everything worse. I know people have arguments, that’s normal, but in those low times it feels like proof that I’ve let everyone down.
Have you ever felt like you’re a failure or that you’ve let yourself or others down, especially during these low periods?

Yes… I mean, I know I already sort of said it, but yes. It’s those little things that turn into a whole court case in my head.

Like the paint—this one tube of pigment, which sounds so silly because people buy things, you know, people buy coffee and shoes and nobody calls a tribunal over it—but I’ll sit there thinking I’ve been selfish, like I’ve somehow ruined the budget or made life harder for everyone. And then if I snap at my spouse, even just a sharp tone, I’ll replay it for hours. What I said, how my face looked, whether I sounded cruel.

It becomes this feeling like I haven’t just made a small mistake, I’ve… I don’t know, damaged the whole household somehow.
Have you felt a noticeable loss of energy or felt fatigued nearly every day, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

I don’t know that I’d say nearly every day. I mean, I have days where I sit down and then it’s like the chair has decided I live there now, but that might just be me avoiding things.

Fatigue is funny, because my spouse will say, “Are you tired?” and I’ll say no, because I don’t feel sleepy exactly. It’s more like… the sink is full of cups, and I look at it, and then I start thinking about how we have too many mugs, and how one of them has a crack, and then I’m online looking up whether ceramic glaze is toxic—so it’s not really energy, maybe it’s distraction.

So, no, I haven’t clearly noticed being physically tired or drained nearly every day. Not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think.
Have you had days where you felt down or depressed most of the time, and it seemed like the sadness wouldn’t go away, even when nothing bad was happening?

Yes… there are stretches like that. Not necessarily because something happened, that’s the strange part.

It’s like the whole house feels gray and heavy, even if the weather is fine or nobody’s upset with me. I’ll end up sitting at the kitchen table just feeling… empty. And then I notice stupid things, like crumbs near the toaster or the way the mail piles up, and I start thinking I should reorganize that drawer with all the rubber bands—sorry, that’s not really the point.

The point is, yes, sometimes the sadness just sits there, like it doesn’t need a reason.

patient.answer:
Yes… there are stretches like that. Not necessarily because something happened, that’s the strange part.

It’s like the whole house feels gray and heavy, even if the weather is fine or nobody’s upset with me. I’ll end up sitting at the kitchen table just feeling… empty. And then I notice stupid things, like crumbs near the toaster or the way the mail piles up, and I start thinking I should reorganize that drawer with all the rubber bands—sorry, that’s not really the point.

The point is, yes, sometimes the sadness just sits there, like it doesn’t need a reason.
